cycles.name: Armour Build
focuses: Come back from the layoff at a dose your sleep can actually pay for, and build the muscle around both discs starting from session one.
Film your leg press top set in weeks 1, 3 and 5, and get the food and sleep moving. Those two are holding back the size more than any exercise is.

paragraphs: You told me you want to build muscle and get your neck strong so the disc doesn't get worse. Both of those are the right goals and we can do both at once. The neck work isn't a separate rehab project sitting next to your training. It is your training.

Here is what shapes this block. You play padel five or six days a week and you sleep five or six hours. That is already a lot of work for your body to recover from. So the gym is only three sessions and each one is short and sharp. I am not going to bury your legs, padel already does that. The sets go where padel gives you nothing, which is your back, your shoulders and your neck. That is also where shape actually shows on you.

You have two discs on record, your neck and your low back. Neither of them is angry right now and I want to keep it that way. So nothing sits on your shoulders this cycle and nothing goes overhead. That isn't me being careful with you. It's me taking the two positions that carry a risk out of the picture so you can push hard on everything else, and you will be pushing hard.
By the end of five weeks I want your rows heavier than they start, your neck holds longer, and three sessions a week that became normal instead of something you have to think about.
outcomes: Chest-supported row heavier at the end than the start
Neck holds every session, plus the daily one at home
Leg press top set filmed in weeks 1, 3 and 5
Three gym sessions a week alongside your padel
Protein hit on five days out of seven
Both discs still quiet at the end of the block

cycles.name: Volume Engine
focuses: The first real size block, aimed at your upper back, shoulders, chest and your weaker side. All the tissue five hundred minutes of padel never builds.
Vertical pull becomes the number we chase, since pressing overhead stays out. Calves and adductors come back in, and the trunk-supported hinge starts carrying real load.
cycles.teaser:
Cycle 1 is where you earn the right to train hard. Cycle 2 is where you actually do it.

More sets, more size, and the first block where the tape measure moves. Your back and shoulders get the attention, because that is what changes how you look at 68 kilos.

Get through five clean weeks and I open the taps.

The armour comes first. Then we build on it.

cycles.name: Density Forge
focuses: Same work, less time. Paired exercises and longer stretches under load, because your limit is the clock and not the exercise list.
The neck work steps up from holding long to holding hard, still nothing bending backwards. The free hinge finally enters, pattern first before any load.

cycles.name: Axis Reclaim
focuses: Heavy comes back to your legs, carried on your hips or by a machine and never across your shoulders. Reps drop, volume drops, and you go after a real five rep number.
This block earns its place by making you strong, and by leaving you fresh for the biggest size block of the whole plan right after it.

cycles.name: Structural Build
focuses: The biggest block of the twenty five weeks, and it comes last on purpose. Twenty weeks of consistency, better food and a proven heavy pattern behind you.
If your sleep and bodyweight have moved by then, this block goes big. If they haven't, it stays where it is and we put the extra into load instead.

days.completionMessage: First session of the week and the one that matters most. Your neck got worked before anything else was allowed to tire you out. Eat something with protein in it tonight.

good: Steady, easy pace
Feel the body warm up, breathing still easy
bad: Don't race it, this is a ramp not a workout

good: Slide your head straight back over your shoulders
Feel the front of your neck switch on
bad: Don't tip your head back

good: Keep your wrists and elbows on the wall as you slide up
Feel your shoulder blades turning upward
bad: Stop before your ribs flare or your chin pushes forward

good: Pull the band apart at chest height
Feel the back of your shoulders
bad: Don't shrug up toward your ears

exercises.name: Loaded Pull Primer
exercises.note: Light weight on both of these. This is still your warm-up, you're just doing it with something in your hands instead of on the floor. Pick a load you could double the reps with. Nothing here should feel like a working set.

good: Keep your arms long and sweep the bar down to your thighs
Feel your lats switch on before you row
bad: Don't bend forward at the waist to push it down

good: Same chest-on-the-pad setup as your working sets
Feel the groove before the weight matters
bad: Don't turn this into a heavy set, it's a rehearsal

exercises.name: Hand-Resisted Neck Hold
exercises.note: This runs first, before anything has tired you out. Three directions only. Hand on your forehead and press forward, then hand on the left side of your head, then the right. Never push backwards. Your head should not actually move, you are just matching the pressure. Start gentle. If anything travels down your arm, or you get pins and needles, stop the set and tell me.

good: Match your hand's pressure so nothing actually moves
Feel the front and sides of the neck switch on
bad: Never press backwards into extension

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.note: This is the lift I want to see move over the five weeks. Your chest stays glued to the pad the whole set. That pad is what keeps your low back out of it, so the second you start rocking to move the weight, it's too heavy. Keep your forehead relaxed and your neck long. If the bench is taken, use the plate-loaded row machine instead.

good: Drive your elbows back into your pockets
Feel the squeeze between your shoulder blades
bad: Don't lift your chest off the pad to move the weight

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.note: Sit tall and stay close to upright. A big lean back turns this into a low back exercise and yours doesn't need the work. Keep your chin tucked and don't crane your neck up to watch the bar.

good: Pull the handle down to your collarbone
Feel it under the armpit, along the outside of your back
bad: Don't lean back and pull with your low back

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
exercises.note: Set the pulley at eye height or just below it, never above your head. This one is doing more for your neck than it looks like it is, so don't rush the reps.

good: Pull the rope apart toward your forehead
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears as you pull
bad: Don't push your chin forward to meet the rope

good: Press straight out and stop the cable turning you
Feel your side abs holding you square
bad: Don't let your back arch as you press

days.focusTag: Drive The Legs, Own The Hinge
days.completionMessage: Your legs got real work without anything sitting on your spine, and your low back got stronger instead of just protected. Keep tonight easy and get some food in.

good: Steady, easy pace
Feel the legs wake up
bad: Don't race it, this is a ramp not a workout

good: Slide your head straight back over your shoulders
Feel the front of your neck switch on
bad: Don't tip your head back

good: Push the floor away through your heels
Feel your glutes, not your low back
bad: Don't arch your back to get higher

good: Turn both knees down to the floor on each side
Feel the stretch deep in the hip
bad: Don't force the range, go where it's comfortable

exercises.name: Loaded Leg Primer
exercises.note: Light on both. The leg press rounds are where you set the seat and find your depth stop for the day, so get that right while the weight is still easy. Then two easy sets of the pull-through to groove the hinge before you load it properly later.

good: Set the seat and find your depth stop with a light load
Feel your low back stay flat on the pad the whole way
bad: Don't chase depth here, this is where you practise stopping

good: Push your hips straight back and keep your back flat
Feel your hamstrings load before you go heavier later
bad: Don't round your low back to reach further

exercises.name: Machine Leg Press
exercises.note: The depth is the whole thing on this lift. Set the seat so your low back is flat against the pad, then find the point where your hips start to curl up off it and stop a hand's width above that. Never go deeper looking for a stretch. Film your top set in weeks 1, 3 and 5 and send it to me. The weight doesn't go up until I've seen it. If the machine is busy use the single leg version, not a goblet squat, not a hack squat, not a Smith machine. Nothing loaded on your shoulders or against your chest.

good: Push the platform away through your whole foot
Feel your thighs and glutes doing the work
bad: Don't let your hips curl up off the pad at the bottom

exercises.name: 45° Back Extension
exercises.note: This one builds the low back rather than protects it, and that's what earns you heavier lifts later. Stop exactly when your body is in a straight line. Don't round down at the bottom and don't keep going into an arch at the top. Both ends matter equally. Bodyweight for the first two weeks. Only add weight once you can do all 12 finishing in a straight line with nothing moving through your spine.

good: Push your hips into the pad and rise until your body is in line
Feel your glutes and hamstrings bring you up
bad: Don't keep going past straight into an arch

good: Drag your heels down and under the seat
Feel the back of your thighs
bad: Don't lift your hips off the seat to finish the rep

exercises.name: Cable Pull Through
exercises.note: This one takes the hip thrust's place and it does the job better for you. Face away from a low pulley, rope between your legs, push your hips straight back until you feel your hamstrings pull, then stand up by squeezing your glutes. The weight pulls you backwards instead of pressing down on you, so your spine gets nothing out of it. Learn this pattern properly now, because it's what earns you a real Romanian deadlift later in the plan.

good: Push your hips straight back and keep your back flat
Feel your hamstrings stretch, then squeeze your glutes to stand tall
bad: Don't round your low back to reach further down

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.note: The small of your back holds one position from the first rep to the last. Not flattened into the floor, not arched off it, just exactly where it starts. Put a hand under there to feel it. If the pressure changes when your leg goes down, bend that knee more and shorten the range until it doesn't. Head stays down on the floor.

good: Reach your opposite arm and leg away from each other
Feel your deep abs stay tight just above your hips
bad: Don't let your back arch off the floor as the leg lowers

days.completionMessage: Shoulders and arms done, and nothing went over your head to get there. That's the whole trick of this day. Good work.

good: Steady, easy pace
Feel the body warm up
bad: Don't race it, this is a ramp not a workout

good: Slide your head straight back over your shoulders
Feel the front of your neck switch on
bad: Don't tip your head back

good: Push your forearms into the wall and slide up
Feel it wrap around your ribs
bad: Stop before your chin pushes forward

good: Keep your elbow pinned to your side and rotate out
Feel the back of the shoulder
bad: Don't let your elbow drift away from your body

exercises.name: Loaded Press Primer
exercises.note: Light weight on both. Face pulls first so your shoulder blades are switched on before anything presses, then two easy rounds on the dumbbells to find the groove. Pulley at eye height or below, same as always.

good: Pull the rope apart toward your forehead
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears
bad: Don't set the pulley above your head

good: Kick the dumbbells up one at a time, same as your working sets
Feel the upper chest and shoulder warm through
bad: Don't go heavy here, you've got three real sets coming

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.note: Getting the dumbbells into place is the risky bit, not the pressing. Sit with them on your knees, kick them up one at a time, and get braced before your first rep. At the end put them down on your thighs one side at a time. Never just drop them from the top. If your shoulder or neck doesn't like it on the day, use the incline chest press machine instead.

good: Press the dumbbells up and slightly together
Feel the upper chest stretch at the bottom
bad: Don't arch your low back off the bench to press

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Landmine Press
exercises.note: This is your overhead press for the whole cycle. The bar stays out in front of your face the whole way, so your head never has to travel back. That's exactly why you're doing this one instead of a shoulder press. Squeeze the glute of your down leg to stop your low back arching as you push.

good: Push the bar up and away, and keep looking straight ahead
Feel the front of the shoulder driving
bad: Don't lean back or arch to get it up

good: Pull the handle to the side of your ribs
Feel the middle of your back
bad: Don't twist your body to help the pull

good: Lead with your elbow out to the side
Feel the side of the shoulder
bad: Don't shrug, keep the shoulder away from your ear

good: Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder
Feel the front of the arm
bad: Don't swing your body to start the rep

cards.title: Why Only Three Days
cards.body:
You play padel five or six days a week and you sleep five or six hours. Your body is already doing a lot of recovering before we add anything. So the gym is three short sessions, and every set in it has to earn its place.

That is why your legs get less than you'd expect. Padel already hammers them every day. What padel gives you nothing for is your upper back, your shoulders and your neck, so that is where most of your sets went. It's also where size actually shows on you.

Some things are at zero this block and I want you to know that's a choice, not an oversight. Calves, inner thigh work and direct triceps come back in Cycle 2. I'd rather do five things properly in 45 minutes than nine things badly.

cards.title: How To Pick Your Weight
cards.body:
I don't give you a weight. You find it. Every exercise gives you the reps and an RPE number, and RPE just means how hard the set should feel. RPE 8 means you finish the set with about two good reps left in you. RPE 7 means about three left.

For anything you've never done before, and the leg press, the landmine press and the pull-through are all new to you, start lighter than you think. Do the first set, see how it felt, then go up. Wasting one light set is much better than picking too heavy and grinding.

Week to week it's simple:

  • You hit all your reps and it felt at or under the target RPE, put a small jump on next week.
  • You were at the RPE ceiling or you missed reps, keep the same weight and do it again.

Going lighter is not failing. If you slept badly or a set is grinding harder than the number says it should, drop the weight. That's you reading your body correctly, which is exactly what I want.

cards.title: Your Warm-Up, Rebuilt
cards.body:
You told me you don't enjoy the floor drills, so I've cut them back to the ones that are actually doing something and given you weight in your hands about four minutes in.

Every day now runs the same way. Bike, one short round of prep, then a loaded primer you log like any other set. Two easy rounds at RPE 6 of the movements you're about to train properly. That primer is not filler, it's how you find your leg press depth and your row groove before the weight is heavy enough to punish a bad one.

The chin tucks stayed and they went up to 16. One round instead of two, same total either way, because those are for your neck and your neck is the whole point of this block.

One thing I won't move: don't skip the primer to save time. It is the warm-up. Going straight into a heavy chest-supported row cold is how a quiet disc stops being quiet.

cards.title: Week One And Week Five
cards.body:
You've had a few weeks off, so week 1 is a calibration week. Cap every RPE at 6. That means every set finishes feeling like you had four more in you. It will feel too easy. Do it anyway. You're finding your weights and letting your body remember the movements.

From week 2 you train to the numbers printed on the cards.

Week 5 is a back-off week. Every RPE drops to 6, and nothing goes below 6. Same exercises, same reps, lighter weights. That week is what lets you start Cycle 2 fresh instead of dug into a hole.

cards.title: Your Neck Plan
cards.body:
You came to me about your neck before it became a bigger problem, and that was the right call. Most people wait. So the neck work isn't sitting off to the side, it's built into every session.

Two parts. The chin tucks in every warm-up train the deep muscles at the front of your neck, and those respond to doing them often rather than doing them hard. Then the neck holds on Day 1 run first, before anything else has tired you out.

Three directions only. Forwards, left and right. Never backwards, not in this cycle and not later. Pushing your head back against resistance is the one thing I don't want you doing with a disc at C5 and C6.

One more thing, and it takes 90 seconds. Do the same holds at home on the days you don't train. Hand on your head, 20 seconds each of the three directions. That's what turns three days a week into every day.

cards.title: When To Stop, When To Keep Going
cards.body:
You've got two discs on record, your neck at C5 and C6 and your low back at L4 and L5. Both are quiet right now. Here's how to keep it that way without being scared of training.

Normal and fine, keep going: muscles burning, feeling tired, being stiff the next day. That's training working.

Not fine: sharp pain. Anything travelling down your arm or down your leg. Numbness or pins and needles anywhere. Pain that builds through a set instead of staying the same.

What to do:

  • Mild and it fades: finish the set, write it in your log.
  • It's building, or it changes how you're moving: stop that exercise, use the swap in its note, message me.
  • Sharp, travelling, numb, or just unfamiliar: stop the session and message me before the next one.

And read this bit properly. Telling me something hurts gets you a modification, never a ban. I change the exercise, the range or the load. I don't take your training away and I don't stop you playing padel. Hiding it from me is the only thing that actually costs you time.

cards.title: Film Your Leg Press
cards.body:
The leg press is the one lift in this block where depth matters more than weight, and I'm not standing next to you. So film your top set in weeks 1, 3 and 5 and send it to me on WhatsApp. Film from the side so I can see your hips.

What I'm checking is one thing. Whether your hips stay flat on the pad at the bottom, or whether they start curling up. That curl is exactly the position your low back doesn't want under load.

The weight goes up on the leg press only after I've seen the film and cleared it. If the videos stop coming, the weight stops moving.

For the sets you don't film, use this: set up, go down until you feel your low back just start to lift off the pad, then come back a hand's width. That's your depth for the whole block.

cards.title: Gym Days And Padel Days
cards.body:
You'll be doing both on the same day most weeks, so here's the rule. Gym after padel, or leave at least four to six hours between them. Lifting first makes you slower and sloppier on court, and sloppy on court is where things get tweaked.

If the two are stuck back to back with no gap, don't skip. Do the warm-up, the neck holds, and the first main lift, then leave. Cap that lift at RPE 6. That's a real session and it keeps the week alive.

Same rule on a day where you're wrecked or you slept badly. Take 1 off every RPE, but never go below 6. Anything already at 6 stays at 6.

You can move the days around to fit your padel. Just keep a day between Day 1 and Day 3. If you only get two sessions in a week, make Day 1 one of them.

cards.title: The Part That Isn't Training
cards.body:
I'll be straight with you. You're 68 kilos, you eat inconsistently, and you sleep five or six hours. You could run this programme perfectly for five weeks and not gain much at all. The training isn't what's limiting you right now. Those two things are.

I'm not going to give you a diet. I'm going to give you two things to hit:

  • Protein at every meal, five days out of seven. A palm-sized portion. Eggs, chicken, yoghurt, meat, whatever you already eat. Just make sure it's there.
  • Half an hour more sleep. Not eight hours, I know your life doesn't allow that. Thirty minutes. Go to bed half an hour earlier four nights a week.

Track both in the habit app. If those two move over these five weeks, Cycle 2 gets to be a proper size block. If they don't, I have to keep the volume where it is, and you'll grow slower than you want to. Your call, and I'd rather tell you now than at the end.
